prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet: the BLOCK animation of the KNIGHT, a slow, heavily armoured warrior behind a huge tower shield, for a Doom/Hexen-style first-person game where monsters are drawn as sprites from several camera angles. It plays for a third of a second when a spell (a fire bolt) strikes the shield and splashes off it. It must read at a glance as "the shield stopped it", not as being hurt.

REFERENCE IMAGES, in the order attached:
1. The knight's turnaround sheet (front, front three-quarter, side, rear three-quarter, back). It is the character design: the battered dark iron plate with rust, the great helm with its narrow eye slit and two pale-blue glints, the torn faded green tabard, the chainmail skirt, the tall oak-and-iron TOWER SHIELD with its round boss and faded pale cross on the LEFT arm, the flanged iron mace in the RIGHT hand, and the shading style.
2. The knight standing, seen from THIS sheet's camera view. Match its camera angle, the way it faces, its pixel size, outline weight, scale and ground line exactly.

The shield stays on the left arm and the mace in the right hand in every frame. Never swap them, and never draw a second shield or a third arm.

LAYOUT
- One horizontal row of 3 equal cells, read left to right, each cell as wide as reference 2.
- Cell 1 is a plain copy of reference 2: the knight standing, exactly as tall, in exactly the same pose. It sets the scale for the other two.
- Cells 2 and 3 are the two block frames described below, drawn at the same scale as cell 1.
- Background: flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, with no gradient, texture, vignette, glow, cast shadow or floor.
- The cells are separated by thin vertical lines of pure cyan (#00FFFF), each running the full height of the image.
- The feet and the shield's bottom edge rest on the same ground line in every cell. The knight does not hop, float or step off the ground.
- The whole figure, including the shield's top and the mace, fits inside each cell with a clear magenta margin. Nothing touches a cell edge or a cyan line, and nothing is cropped.
- No text, labels, numbers, frame borders, speed lines, motion blur, sparks, fire, smoke or impact effects. Only the knight; the game draws the spell and its splash itself.
- Crisp pixel art with hard edges and no anti-aliasing against the magenta. No semi-transparent pixels, and no pink or purple glow bleeding into the background.

THE BLOCK: the spell strikes the shield's face from in front of the knight.
- Cell 2, IMPACT: the instant of the hit. The knight hunkers down behind the shield, knees bent, the shield pushed forward and a little up, braced on the left forearm and with the right shoulder driven against its back; the helm ducks down so only its crown and the eye slit peek over the shield's top edge. The shield's face is lit brighter and hotter along its rim and boss, as if the fire just splashed off it (light on the iron and wood only, no flames or sparks in the air). The mace arm is pulled in tight behind the shield.
- Cell 3, BRACE: a moment later. Still crouched low behind the raised shield, firm and unshaken, the shield's face back to its normal colours, the eye slit glinting over the rim, the mace arm still tucked in. The knight is a little lower than standing in both frames.
VIEW: front, as in the first cell of reference 1 and in reference 2. The knight faces the viewer squarely in every cell, the shield's face toward us. The shield is on the knight's left arm, the IMAGE-RIGHT side of its body's centre, wide enough to hide the body; the mace arm is on the IMAGE-LEFT side.
- Cell 2: the shield is pushed toward the viewer and a little up, so it looks slightly bigger and its bottom edge lifts just off the ground; behind it the knight crouches, and only the helm's crown and eye slit show over the top edge. The mace arm is drawn in behind the shield, only the mace head showing at its image-left edge. The rim and the boss glow hot orange, fading into the wood.
- Cell 3: the same crouch behind the raised shield, its bottom edge back on the ground, the colours back to normal; the eye slit glints over the top edge.
